headline: CBA's cash NPAT rose 6% to $5,445 million in 1H26 (vs $5,132 million in 1H25). Statutory NPAT was $5,412 million. Total operating income grew 7% to $15,021 million, driven by a $761 million increase in NII and a $163 million rise in other operating income. Operating performance increased $406 million to $8,131 million, supported by underlying expense growth of $348 million and notable items of $170 million. Loan impairment expense decreased marginally by $1 million to $319 million.

drivers.narrative: NII increased $761 million or 6% on the prior comparative period. The result was driven by a $96 billion or 8% increase in average interest earning assets to $1,232 billion, partly offset by a 4 basis point decrease in net interest margin to 2.04%. Home loan balances increased $31 billion, while business and corporate loans grew $29 billion.

Other operating income increased $163 million or 8% to $2,326 million. Commissions rose $61 million to $1,146 million, lending fees increased $16 million to $465 million, trading income grew $84 million to $603 million, and funds management income increased $7 million to $67 million.

Underlying operating expenses increased $348 million or 5% to $6,720 million. Staff expenses rose $169 million to $4,139 million, information technology services expenses increased $134 million to $1,321 million, and other expenses grew $40 million to $795 million.
Restructuring and notable items were $170 million in 1H26, compared to nil in 1H25. This represents an additional negative contribution of $170 million to earnings.

Loan impairment expense decreased by $1 million to $319 million. Business Banking saw a decrease of $129 million to an expense of $91 million, Institutional Banking and Markets saw a decrease of $17 million to a benefit of $8 million, and New Zealand saw a decrease of $12 million to an expense of $4 million, partially offset by an increase in Retail Banking Services of $153 million to an expense of $232 million.

Corporate tax expense increased $94 million or 4% to $2,367 million, reflecting a 30.3% effective tax rate compared to 30.7% in the prior period. The decrease in the effective tax rate was primarily due to a decrease in non-deductible expenses.

notable_items: Restructuring and notable items: $170 million in 1H26 vs nil in 1H25.
limitations: Capped at 80: operating_expenses -348 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.

evidence_records.quote: Non-cash items are excluded from net profit after tax (“cash basis”), which is management’s preferred measure of the Group’s financial performance, as they tend to be non-recurring in nature or are not considered representative of the Group’s ongoing financial performance.
The impact of these items on the Group’s net profit after tax (“statutory basis”) is outlined below and treated consistently with the prior financial year.

These amounts include post-completion adjustments (such as purchase price adjustments, and finalisation of accounting adjustments for goodwill and foreign currency reserves recycling), and transaction and separation costs associated with the previously announced divestments.

Hedging and IFRS volatility represents timing differences between fair value movements on qualifying economic hedges and the underlying exposure. They do not affect the Group’s performance over the life of the hedge relationship, and are recognised over the life of the hedged transaction.
